arguments.value: This agreement says Seattle Software Developers will build Pelican Delivers’ application phase 1 under one or more statements of work. The developer must design, code, test, and deliver the software and related documentation by agreed milestones, and the client must test each milestone and accept it or send a written change request within set time limits. If there are requested changes or extra work, both sides must approve a written change order before the developer has to do the extra work. The client pays the agreed fees, expenses if applicable, and possibly a bonus for early completion, and failure to pay is a material breach. The completed software and related work are treated as work made for hire, so the client owns the final product, while the developer keeps ownership of its preexisting tools and technology. Both sides must keep confidential information secret, and breaches can be stopped by court order. The developer is an independent contractor, the client is responsible for legal compliance on its business side, and each party gives certain warranties and agrees to indemnify the other for specified claims. Either party can end the agreement with two weeks’ notice, or immediately for material breach, nonpayment, confidentiality violations, or unlawful conduct. If the agreement ends, the client pays for work already done and the developer must hand over the work product and may provide paid transition assistance. Washington law governs the agreement, disputes go to courts in King County, and the agreement is the full final understanding between the parties.
